cohort: The study included 200 women with singleton pregnancies beyond 37 weeks, divided into 100 high-risk and 100 normal pregnancies.
finding: Non-reactive admission cardiotocography (CTG) was more common in high-risk pregnancies and was associated with poorer neonatal outcomes (lower Apgar scores, higher NICU admissions), though CTG had restricted sensitivity (52%) and an elevated false positive rate (21%).
mod_finding: Cesarean section was necessitated in 54% of high-risk pregnancies compared to 24% of normal pregnancies.
